pressure_gas_history: Rapid cabin depressurization. Descended to approximately 3,000 m within five minutes and landed about 30 minutes after the incident. Supplemental oxygen was available to and used by the flight crew only. Continuous pressure and individual gas delivery are unreported.
outcome_ascertainment: Figure 1 places initial priority presentations at about 20 h and completion of triage at about 24 h. Specialty assessment was selective. Five patients received hyperbaric treatment at about 31 h and one at about 72 h. Four of six treated patients initially attended specialty follow-up. Planned MRI for one of those four was not completed.
locator: Printed pp. 1086–1087, Figure 1 and case report

pressure_gas_history: Sudden depressurization about three hours into the flight. Passengers and crew breathed supplemental oxygen until descending below 3,049 m in less than five minutes. The aircraft landed in Bahrain. Continuous pressure and individual gas delivery are unreported.
outcome_ascertainment: All occupants were screened and monitored for 72 h as described by the author. Cases A and B had onset 30–60 min after the excursion. The author describes case C's onset at about 3 h and a presumptive spinal diagnosis. Case D was identified later with exact symptom onset unreported. The source lists approximately 60 passengers and six crew. Case-to-role linkage is unavailable.
locator: Printed pp. 429–431, event narrative and cases A–D
